blocks.text: Referral to a nephrologist is indicated in the following situations:
Reduced kidney function: eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage G3 or worse) or rapid decline in eGFR (>5 mL/min/1.73 m² per year).
Significant albuminuria/proteinuria: Persistent urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) ≥30 mg/g on at least two occasions, nephrotic-range proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), or nephrotic syndrome.

Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a clinical diagnosis based on the presence of albuminuria, reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), or both in patients with diabetes mellitus. It includes diabetic nephropathy, which classically presents with microalbuminuria (30–300 mg/g or 3–30 mg/mmol) and diabetic retinopathy.

with microalbuminuria (30–300 mg/g or 3–30 mg/mmol) and diabetic retinopathy.

blocks.text: DKD typically develops after long-standing diabetes (usually >10 years in type 1 diabetes) but may be present at the time of diagnosis in type 2 diabetes. It may also occur without retinopathy or without albuminuria, particularly in type 2 diabetes. Alternative causes of kidney disease should be considered when atypical features are present.
